blueprint.name: Common Law Admission Test
blueprint.source: CLAT: 120 questions, 120 marks, 120 minutes; negative 0.25. Section counts vary by year, so this split is provisional.

questions.text: The scientist's hypothesis was initially met with ______ by the academic community, but subsequent experiments provided compelling evidence that forced a reconsideration.
questions.solution: Shortcut: The contrast marker 'but' signals a shift from negative to positive; eliminate positive/neutral words. Step-by-step: The phrase 'forced a reconsideration' implies the initial reaction was doubtful, so 'skepticism' fits; 'enthusiasm' and 'acclaim' are opposite, 'indifference' doesn't lead to reconsideration.

questions.text: The landing site of the Chandrayaan-3 Vikram lander on the Moon's south polar region was officially named by the Prime Minister of India on August 26, 2023. What is the designated name of this landing site?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate options named after the lander (Vikram) or rover (Pragyan) as sites are usually given distinct symbolic names. 'Tiranga Point' was the Chandrayaan-2 crash site. The correct name 'Shiv Shakti' signifies welfare and strength. Step-by-step: PM Modi announced the name 'Shiv Shakti Point' during his visit to ISRO Telemetry Tracking and Command Network (ISTRAC) in Bengaluru on Aug 26, 2023. 'Tiranga Point' marks the Chandrayaan-2 impact site (2019). Vikram is the lander module; Pragyan is the rover.

questions.text: Parliament enacts the Constitution (Fiftieth Amendment) Act, inserting a new Article 329B which reads: 'Notwithstanding anything in this Constitution, no election to either House of Parliament or to the House or either House of the Legislature of a State shall be called in question in any Court of Law.' The Amendment is challenged in the Supreme Court on the ground that it violates the 'Basic Structure' of the Constitution.

options.label: A
options.text: The Amendment is invalid as it destroys the 'Basic Structure' of the Constitution by completely ousting judicial review in election matters, which is a fundamental feature of the Constitution.

options.label: B
options.text: The Amendment is valid because Parliament's constituent power under Article 368 is plenary and unfettered, allowing it to amend any provision of the Constitution including those relating to elections.

options.label: C
options.text: The Amendment is valid only if it has been ratified by the Legislatures of not less than one-half of the States as per the proviso to Article 368(2).

options.label: D
options.text: The Amendment is invalid solely because it violates Article 14 (Right to Equality) by creating an arbitrary classification between election disputes and other disputes.

questions.solution: Shortcut: 'Judicial Review' is a core Basic Structure feature (Kesavananda Bharati); any amendment removing court jurisdiction over election disputes (free & fair elections) is unconstitutional per se, regardless of majority or ratification. Step-by-step: 1. Identify the amendment's effect: Total exclusion of judicial scrutiny of elections. 2. Recall Basic Structure doctrine: Judicial Review, Free & Fair Elections, Democracy are basic features. 3. Eliminate B (Parliament's power is limited by Basic Structure). 4. Eliminate C (Ratification requirement applies to federal provisions; Basic Structure violation cannot be cured by ratification). 5. Eliminate D (The primary ground is Basic Structure destruction, not merely Art 14 violation). 6. Option A correctly captures the ratio of *Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain* and subsequent jurisprudence.

questions.text: The price of an article is increased by 20% and then decreased by 20%. What is the net percentage change in the price?
questions.solution: Shortcut: For successive increase and decrease by the same percentage x%, the net percentage change is -x²/100%. Here x = 20, so net change = -400/100 = -4% (a 4% decrease). Full solution: Assume original price = 100. After 20% increase, price = 120. After 20% decrease, price = 120 × 0.8 = 96. The final price is 96, which is a 4% decrease from the original 100.

questions.text: Dr. Rao, a renowned cardiologist, visits City Hospital twice a week to perform surgeries. The hospital provides the operation theatre, nursing staff, anaesthetists, and equipment. During a surgery, Dr. Rao negligently leaves a surgical swab inside the patient, causing sepsis. The patient sues City Hospital for damages. The hospital contends that Dr. Rao is an independent contractor exercising his professional skill, for whose negligence the hospital cannot be held vicariously liable.

options.label: A
options.text: The hospital is not liable because Dr. Rao is an independent contractor exercising exclusive professional judgment, and the hospital lacked control over his surgical technique.

options.label: B
options.text: The hospital is liable under the doctrine of vicarious liability as Dr. Rao was integrated into the hospital's functioning for patient care, and the hospital owes a non-delegable duty of care to its patients.

options.label: C
options.text: The hospital is liable only if it is proven that the hospital administration was negligent in verifying Dr. Rao's medical credentials before granting him visiting privileges.

options.label: D
options.text: The hospital is not liable because the negligence occurred during the exercise of Dr. Rao's specialized professional skill, which falls outside the hospital's right of control.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Modern vicarious liability for hospitals uses the 'integration/organization test' and 'non-delegable duty of care' — hospitals cannot escape liability for negligence of doctors integrated into their patient care system by labeling them independent contractors. Step-by-step: 1. Identify the relationship: Hospital provides infrastructure/team; Doctor performs core function (surgery). 2. Apply principle: Courts hold hospitals liable for visiting consultants under 'ostensible agency' or 'non-delegable duty' (e.g., *M/s. Spring Meadows Hospital v. Harjol Ahluwalia*). 3. Eliminate A & D (rely on outdated 'control test' for independent contractors). 4. Eliminate C (negligent selection is a separate/direct liability, not the sole basis for vicarious liability). 5. Option B correctly states the current legal position.

questions.text: Find the next term in the series: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The differences between consecutive terms increase by 2 each time (4, 6, 8, 10). The next difference is 12, so add 12 to the last term. Step‑by‑step: 2+4=6, 6+6=12, 12+8=20, 20+10=30, 30+12=42.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Each of the participants in the workshop (A) / have confirmed their attendance (B) / for the valedictory session (C) / scheduled on Friday evening. (D)

options.label: A
options.text: Each of the participants in the workshop

questions.solution: Shortcut: 'Each of + plural noun/pronoun' always takes a singular verb. Spot 'Each of' → verb must be singular (has/is/was). Option B uses plural 'have' → error. Full solution: The subject is 'Each' (singular); 'of the participants' is a prepositional phrase modifying it. The verb must agree with 'Each', so 'has confirmed' is correct. Option B incorrectly uses 'have confirmed'. The pronoun 'their' is acceptable as singular 'they' in modern usage. Segments A, C, and D are grammatically sound.

questions.text: In the context of India's space exploration efforts, which organization successfully launched the 'Chandrayaan-4' mission preparation phase or related precursor missions aimed at establishing a permanent human presence on the Moon?

options.label: A
options.text: The National Space Organization (NSO) of China.

questions.solution: Chandrayaan is a series of lunar exploration missions developed and launched by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). While ISRO has launched Chandrayaan-1 and Chandrayaan-3, it is the agency responsible for India's broader lunar program and future preparations. The other options refer to space agencies from China, Europe, and Japan respectively, none of which are associated with the 'Chandrayaan' naming convention or India's specific lunar mission architecture.

questions.text: During a laparoscopic cholecystectomy (gallbladder removal), the surgeon inadvertently severs the patient's common bile duct, a structure adjacent to the surgical site but not intended to be operated upon. The patient suffers permanent liver damage. The hospital records show the surgery was recorded, but the footage is 'corrupted' and unavailable. The surgeon asserts there is no direct evidence of *how* the error occurred. The patient pleads that the injury itself implies negligence. Which legal maxim enables the court to shift the burden of proof to the defendant in such circumstances?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Apply the 'Res Ipsa Loquitur' (The thing speaks for itself) checklist: (1) Instrumentality under defendant's exclusive control, (2) Accident does not ordinarily occur without negligence, (3) No voluntary contribution by plaintiff. If all three met, burden shifts to defendant. Full Solution: Severing the common bile duct during a routine gallbladder surgery is an event that does not ordinarily happen if due care is exercised (satisfying condition 2). The surgical instruments and field were under the exclusive control of the surgical team (condition 1). The unconscious patient contributed nothing (condition 3). Since direct evidence (video) is unavailable due to the hospital's custody, the maxim *Res Ipsa Loquitur* applies, creating a rebuttable presumption of negligence. *Res Judicata* bars re-litigation; *Volenti* is voluntary assumption of risk; *Caveat Emptor* applies to buyer-seller transactions.

rows: Bile duct severance rare in standard procedure

questions.text: Rearrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph: 1. The novel's protagonist, a disillusioned journalist, returns to his hometown after two decades. 2. He discovers that the once-familiar streets now bear the scars of unchecked industrialization. 3. His investigation into a local environmental scandal reignites his sense of purpose. 4. The narrative explores themes of redemption and the cost of progress. Choose the correct sequence.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Identify the opening sentence (introduces protagonist) and closing sentence (thematic summary); then sequence the middle events chronologically. Step-by-step: Sentence 1 introduces the journalist's return; sentence 2 describes the changed setting he observes; sentence 3 narrates his subsequent investigation; sentence 4 provides the thematic overview. Thus the logical order is 1-2-3-4.

questions.text: A State Legislature enacts the 'Agricultural Produce Moneylending Regulation Act, 2023', capping interest rates charged by moneylenders to farmers. The Union Government challenges the Act, contending that 'Banking' (Entry 45, Union List) covers all lending activities, rendering the State law ultra vires. The State argues the legislation, in its true nature and character, regulates 'Money Lending' (Entry 30, State List) and 'Agricultural Indebtedness'. Which constitutional doctrine is the primary test to determine the validity of the State legislation in this scenario?
questions.solution: Shortcut: When a law's legislative competence is challenged due to overlap between Union and State List entries, apply the 'Pith and Substance' test: identify the *true nature and character* of the law by examining its object, scope, and effect. If the core falls within the enacting legislature's list, incidental encroachment is permissible. Full Solution: The dispute centers on whether the State law on moneylending encroaches on the Union's 'Banking' power. The Supreme Court consistently holds (e.g., *State of Bombay v. F.N. Balsara*) that the doctrine of Pith and Substance determines validity by analyzing the legislation's dominant purpose. Here, the Act targets agricultural indebtedness and local moneylending, squarely falling under Entry 30 (State List). Incidental trenching on 'Banking' does not invalidate it. Colourable Legislation applies to *mala fide* attempts to legislate beyond power; Eclipse deals with pre-constitutional laws; Severability deals with separating valid/invalid portions of a statute.
questions.topic: Constitutional Law - Distribution of Legislative Powers

questions.text: Find the missing term in the following series: 5, 11, 23, 47, 95, ?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Differences are 6, 12, 24, 48 (doubling each time); add 96 to 95. Step-by-step: Consecutive differences: 11-5=6, 23-11=12, 47-23=24, 95-47=48. The differences form a geometric progression multiplying by 2. Next difference = 48 × 2 = 96. Missing term = 95 + 96 = 191. Alternatively, each term follows (Previous × 2) + 1: 95 × 2 + 1 = 191.

questions.text: The landing site of the Chandrayaan-3 Vikram lander near the Moon's south pole was officially named 'Shiv Shakti Point' by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2024. Which of the following sites is associated with the Chandrayaan-2 mission's hard landing?
questions.solution: Shortcut (Option Elimination): 'Shiv Shakti Point' is Chandrayaan-3 (Option C). 'Jawahar Point' is the Moon Impact Probe site of Chandrayaan-1 (Option B). 'Vikram Sarabhai' is a crater name/person (Option D). 'Tiranga Point' was the name designated for the Chandrayaan-2 Vikram lander impact site. Full Solution: PM Modi announced 'Shiv Shakti Point' for Chandrayaan-3 (Aug 2023) and 'Tiranga Point' for the Chandrayaan-2 crash site. The IAU formally approved 'Shiv Shakti' (Statio Shiv Shakti) in March 2024. Chandrayaan-1's MIP impact site is Jawahar Point.

questions.text: After months of negotiation, the deadlock was finally broken and both parties managed to ______.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Check context clues: 'deadlock broken', 'months of negotiation' imply progress/recovery after difficulty. 'Turn the corner' means to pass the worst point. Eliminate B (ignore), C (personal reform), D (reverse power dynamic). Full Solution: The context describes a breakthrough after a prolonged stalemate. 'Turn the corner' is an idiom meaning to pass a critical or dangerous phase and begin to improve. 'Turn a blind eye' means to ignore deliberately. 'Turn over a new leaf' means to reform one's conduct. 'Turn the tables' means to reverse one's position relative to an opponent. Only Option A fits the context of mutual progress after a crisis.

questions.text: The Supreme Court of India delivered a landmark judgment in November 2024, holding that the right to privacy is a fundamental right protected under Article 21 of the Constitution. In which specific context did the Court affirm this principle most recently, distinguishing it from a mere privilege granted by the State?

options.label: A
options.text: The validity of biometric data collection for voting in local body elections.

options.label: B
options.text: The mandatory installation of surveillance cameras in all private educational institutions.

options.label: C
options.text: The legality of facial recognition technology usage by law enforcement agencies without individual consent.

options.label: D
options.text: The requirement for citizens to disclose their social media passwords to tax authorities.

questions.solution: The correct option is C because the 2024 judgment specifically addressed the boundaries of state surveillance and the use of advanced biometric technologies like facial recognition, reinforcing that such intrusion requires strict procedural safeguards and cannot be arbitrary. Option A is incorrect as voting eligibility is governed by the Representation of the People Act rather than a fundamental right to privacy in this specific context. Option B is wrong because private educational institutions do not have the same level of state interference regarding surveillance mandates without due process, and the judgment did not focus on them. Option D is incorrect because while privacy protects against arbitrary disclosure, the tax laws operate under distinct statutory frameworks that may compel disclosure for verification purposes, which was not the primary subject of the 2024 ruling.
